C-PLATFORM-BROKERED-IO-BOUNDARIES-202609.Summary: Close ambient I/O paths with separate trusted brokers for network egress, credentials, filesystem portals, downloads, and large artifacts, using capability-scoped resources, engine-specific enforcement where required, streaming transport, and metadata-only observability.
C-PLATFORM-BROKERED-IO-BOUNDARIES-202609.Problem: The current request-policy callback does not prove complete network mediation, native same-account processes can reach ambient OS resources, credential handling lacks a non-exportable broker contract, and some download or blob paths can materialize whole files through bounded JSON-style frames. A generated feature could otherwise exfiltrate profile data, bypass browser policy, exhaust memory, or confuse access to metadata with access to bytes.

Goals.Goal: Inventory every egress plane: browser engine, feature host, model and integration providers, updater, browser services, and trusted system processes.
Provide separate network capabilities scoped by destination, protocol, method, redirect policy, origin context, byte budget, and purpose.
Provide non-exportable credential handles scoped to exact provider, account, operation, and destination.
Provide filesystem and artifact portals based on opaque handles rather than host paths.
Stream downloads and large artifacts with chunk, total-size, time, concurrency, digest, and backpressure limits.
Preserve engine-specific request enforcement behind the portable broker contract.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
The architecture decision, effect fence, durable activation, untrusted feature host, and browser gateway changes must define their contracts before this package is planned.
Feature-runtime network, browser-engine network, updater network, and model-provider network are distinct authority planes and cannot share one ambient grant.
Credential values are never returned to ordinary features when the broker can perform the authorized operation on their behalf.
A filesystem path is data, not authority; access requires an opaque portal handle bound to an allowed root, operation, and activation epoch.
Download metadata authority does not imply artifact-byte authority, and artifact-byte authority does not imply arbitrary filesystem write authority.
Browser request policy must be enforced in the real engine path; an advisory callback or reference fixture is not complete egress evidence.
Redirect, DNS rebinding, proxy, service-worker, WebSocket, download, and retry behavior must preserve destination and budget policy.
No raw secrets, page bodies, file contents, queries, URLs with sensitive parameters, or credential handles enter generic telemetry.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Implementing a universal engine-independent network stack.
Giving features raw sockets or host filesystem paths.
UI design for file pickers or permission prompts beyond their broker contract.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: An egress inventory names the authoritative enforcement point and default policy for browser engine, feature host, updater, model, integration, and system-service traffic.
An ordinary feature without a network handle cannot create direct or indirect outbound traffic, including through raw WASI sockets, native helpers, browser debug APIs, or unbrokered service calls.

Network grants constrain destination, resolved address policy, protocol, method, redirects, request and response bytes, concurrency, deadline, and retry class and are revalidated through an effect fence.

Real CEF tests cover navigation and subresource policy, redirects, blocked schemes, service-worker or equivalent mediated paths where supported, and explicit unsupported coverage where interception is unavailable.
Credential broker operations use non-exportable handles and bind provider, account, operation, destination, runtime, and activation epoch; cross-runtime reuse and logging are denied.

Filesystem access is possible only through bounded portal handles and canonicalized roots, with traversal, alternate streams, UNC, symlink or reparse escape, and stale-handle tests appropriate to the target OS.
Downloads use a streaming or chunked data plane with backpressure and total-size quotas and do not buffer an unbounded complete file in one JSON envelope or process heap.
Download metadata, artifact bytes, export destination, and overwrite consent remain separate capabilities.
Digest verification and crash recovery preserve a single authoritative artifact state and classify uncertain external effects as Incomplete.
Metrics record counts, byte budgets, duration, destination class, denial, and outcome without raw secrets or user content.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh negative and real-engine evidence proves separate egress planes, non-exportable credentials, path-free filesystem authority, streaming bounded artifacts, redirect and destination enforcement, and metadata-only diagnostics.

Assumptions.Assumption: Some enforcement must remain engine-specific while presenting common grant and outcome semantics to features.
Existing blob and download contracts can evolve additively to a streaming data plane without exposing host paths.
Updater egress remains system-only and can be independently pinned and audited.
